subject: Cloud Computing
title: Redundancy Is Not Optional
description: A fast breakdown of Redundancy Is Not Optional for builders.

hook.text: A company runs everything in one availability zone. That zone has a power failure. Everything goes down.

buildup.text: Redundancy means running copies of critical services in multiple locations. If one fails, the other takes over.

discovery.text: Cloud makes redundancy accessible: multi-AZ databases, cross-region failover, and global load balancing.

twist.text: Redundancy doubles your cost. Teams that skip it are gambling that nothing will go wrong. They always lose eventually.

climax.text: The question isn't 'will something fail?' but 'when it fails, what happens next?' Redundancy answers that question.

punchline.text: Everything fails eventually. Redundancy decides what happens next.

quiz.question: Why do some teams skip redundancy despite knowing the risks?
options: It doubles costs and teams gamble that failures won't happen to them
Cloud providers guarantee 100% uptime without redundancy
Redundancy is only needed for companies with over 1 million users

details.summary: Every major cloud failure reinforces that redundancy is not optional. Single points of failure in regions, availability zones, services, and providers all eventually fail. Redundancy must be tested regularly because untested failover is not actually redundancy.
details.whyItMatters: It is not a question of if cloud components will fail but when. Redundancy and tested failover are the only reliable protection against inevitable failures.
takeaways: Every cloud component will eventually fail
Redundancy must span zones, regions, and sometimes providers
Untested failover does not count as redundancy

faq.question: What types of redundancy should cloud architectures have?
faq.answer: Multi-AZ for withstanding data center failures, multi-region for surviving regional outages, multi-provider for eliminating single-vendor risk, and application-level redundancy with graceful degradation when any dependency is unavailable.

faq.question: How often should failover be tested?
faq.answer: Critical systems should test failover quarterly at minimum. Game day exercises that simulate real failures in production reveal gaps that theoretical analysis misses. Netflix's Chaos Monkey approach of continuously injecting failures keeps systems resilient through constant testing.
